chapters.category: Aramaic and Ethiopic textual traditions • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 79 — The Completed Account of the Luminaries
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. The Aramaic manuscript 4Q209 (4QEnastrᵇ ar), especially fragments 26–28, is primary for its surviving wording associated with Enoch's address to his son, the revealed reckoning, appointed times, months and courses in verses 1–2. The fragmentary Aramaic text does not preserve complete clauses for the whole chapter, and its lacunae remain unsupplied. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, preserves all six verses and supplies the complete sequence, the moon's sixth-gate decrease, the 177-day and five-day counts, and the concluding description of Uriel. Earlier legible Aramaic readings are followed where they directly correspond; Geʽez supplies everything not extant there. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: And now, my son Methuselah, I have shown you everything, and the whole account of the laws of the stars of heaven is complete.
verses.study: Enoch marks both transmission and completion. Knowledge received through vision is entrusted to his son as an ordered account.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:9 — what has been seen is taught to children and grandchildren
Proverbs 4:3–4 — a father passes received instruction to his son

verses.text: Uriel showed me all their laws for every day and every appointed time, under every rule and in every year: their going out and their command in every month and every week.
verses.study: The laws extend across day, season, year, month and week. The repeated scope presents celestial service as comprehensive and accountable.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — lights govern signs, seasons, days and years
Daniel 2:21 — times and seasons remain under divine authority

verses.text: He showed me the decrease of the moon that takes place at the sixth portal, for at this sixth portal its light is completed, and from it comes the beginning of the month.
verses.study: The ending of lunar light becomes the month's beginning. Completion and renewal meet at the same portal.
crossReferences: Numbers 10:10 — the beginning of months is marked before God
Psalm 104:19 — the moon is appointed for seasons

verses.text: Its decrease takes place at the first portal in its appointed period until 177 days are completed—twenty-five weeks and two days by the reckoning of weeks.
verses.study: The 177-day total is restated as twenty-five weeks plus two days. Two forms of counting verify one period.
crossReferences: Leviticus 23:15–16 — weeks and days are counted together
Daniel 9:24 — weeks can frame a revealed period

verses.text: It falls behind the sun and the ordered course of the stars by exactly five days in one half-year, when this visible station is completed.
verses.study: The lunar reckoning is measured against the sun and stars without merging their courses. The five-day difference emerges at the completed half-year station.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — distinct lights share the work of measuring time
Psalm 90:12 — careful numbering of days serves wisdom

verses.text: This is the appearance and likeness of every light that Uriel, the great angel who leads them, showed me.
verses.study: The chapter ends by naming the disclosure as both appearance and pattern. Uriel's guidance preserves the connection between what Enoch saw and the laws he recorded.
crossReferences: Ezekiel 1:28 — a visible likeness communicates heavenly glory
Revelation 1:1 — an angel makes the revelation known to the seer

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 79 closes the preceding lunar instruction with Enoch's address to Methuselah. The completed account is not private knowledge but teaching handed from father to son.
Uriel's revelation encompasses days, appointed times, years, months and weeks. Every scale of time is connected to the commanded courses of the heavenly lights.
The chapter revisits the moon's decrease at the sixth and first portals, then states 177 days as twenty-five weeks and two days. The five-day difference from the solar half-year remains explicit.
The conclusion identifies Uriel as the great angel leading the lights. Observation, calculation and angelic instruction remain joined in Enoch's testimony.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — lights distinguish time and rule day and night
Psalm 104:19 — the moon serves appointed times
Daniel 2:21 — God governs times and seasons
Daniel 9:24 — weeks form a measured period
Revelation 1:1 — revelation is mediated through an angel
